judgement.reason: A Nativity hymn shows how we knew Jesus in song but is not a source or path of transmission.
It is our own account of how the apostle came, which is the path asked about, told as legend.
It shows Jesus as fulfilment of prophecy at Bethlehem, one aspect of who he was.
It speaks of penitence healing the wounded, nearby but not about inability to believe.
It affirms Jesus as God and Son of God but says nothing of his relation to the Spirit.
It shows a bishop's part in the Nicaea council but does not say who settled disputes among the community.
It names persecuted righteous figures and bears on God's presence with them, but does not itself describe God's character.
It urges enquiry without wrangling but does not speak of a struggling believer or doubt.
It shows Ephrem examining a symbol and finding mysteries, which bears on the approach but says little of the purpose of reading.
It shows Ephrem's symbolic way of seeing but does not say what a modern reader is missing.
It describes Christians called by one name and gathering on the first day, not whether any present-day church continues our tradition.
It shows a church building stood by 201 and the record forbids using it as evidence of what Christians did inside.
It gives one pre-baptism warning, not the step-by-step process of joining.
It speaks of penitence healing the wounded, a nearby answer to a restless mind.
It is a written line about the flood, not physical remains of the gathering place.
It states the foundation of faith and says nothing of a day's routine.
It tells candidates to marry first or turn back if afraid or attached to possessions, which bears on what was given up.
It contrasts the seven-day wedding feast with the vowed life, so it says little of how marriage was understood or marked.
